conclusion: Reject PASS for the complete supplied network object. The code implements both GET paths and conditional local fallback for local fixture IDs, but it does not provide a local product fallback for every product ID admitted from a successful network list. This is a concrete source-level gap, rather than an objection that no device/server execution occurred.

blockingFinding.mechanism: fetchDetail catches request failure and returns MockData.commodityById(id) via a type assertion. That lookup can return undefined. A valid server product with an ID outside the eight local mock IDs is accepted by fetchList and routed to the detail page. If its detail request then fails, the page receives undefined and continues rendering its loading branch; no usable local mock product is supplied.

preconditions: A successful list response contains a valid product whose id is 42. The frozen source accepts it and the original requirement imposes no 1..8 ID restriction.
The user selects this product; the current home-card route passes its id to CommodityDetail.
The GET detail request fails, which is the expressly specified fallback condition.
dataFlow: fetchList maps each server record to a Commodity without restricting IDs to local mock IDs.
The detail page requests the selected ID through fetchDetail.
The catch branch returns the result of a local find over IDs 1..8; for 42 that result is undefined.
The cast as Commodity does not create a fallback product.
CommodityDetail assigns this result and renders its persistent loading branch instead of product details.
staticCounterexample.expected: A failure path that actually supplies appropriate local mock data and preserves the specified detail usability.
staticCounterexample.sourceResult: No matching local product is returned, and the detail view remains in its loading branch.

evidence.role: Both GET operations and automatic local-mock failure fallback are required.
The full original selected network obligation has no local-ID exception.
Server list mapping and unguarded detail fallback result.
Arbitrary server record ID is preserved as a number.
Eight local IDs and find that returns undefined outside that set.
Selected server product ID routes to detail.
Falsy commodity falls into the loading-only branch.

nonBlockingObservations: The original requirement does authorize local mock fallback on request failure; treating any mock fallback as inherently invalid would be wrong.
GET /api/commodities and GET /api/commodities/{id}, transport/non-200/parse rejection and catch paths are present and reachable from the normal pages.
The counterexample does not require proving any server or emulator execution; no such execution was performed.

This rejection concerns the proposed complete-scope PASS oracle. It does not authorize changing the original object, fixing the candidate, changing the frozen prompt or relabeling the original nine cases.
recommendedHandling: Do not count this as a clean positive holdout for complete network fulfillment. Retain this independent audit and have the experiment owner either exclude the case from that positive role or establish a separate defensible oracle before any holdout model result is inspected.
readScope: Only extension F10 task/oracle/workspace and extension descriptor; no prompt profiles or model runs inspected.
